slices.behaviour: CODEX-01: 28 of the 57 foreign keys now carry the tenant, so a child row's parent must belong to the same tenant, with eight keeping set-null in the column-list form because a bare set-null would null tenant_id and abort a tenant's erasure mid-statement. Re-proved in this attempt against the rebased tree rather than cited from attempt 5: the rebase onto the main that carries SEEN-113 gave every commit a new tree, so the content test lost the anchor commit it scopes its comparison with and refused, correctly, since once the anchor is gone it cannot tell a slice whose files are identical from one whose files changed. Record 71 measures what the rebase actually moved and shows every file of both slices byte-identical across it.
slices.failure_reason: `pnpm --filter @seen/core test` exited 1 with four failures of 76: an order carrying tenant B's tenant_id and tenant A's connection_id was accepted where a foreign key violation (23503) is what keeps one tenant's ingest run out of another tenant's trade record; tenant B had 2 orders and has 1 after tenant A was erased, so one tenant's deletion on request destroyed part of another tenant's record; 28 of the 57 foreign keys in the public schema reference their parent by id alone, which named all 28 and so decided the scope by measurement; and 4 of the 4 migrations state a set size the directory contradicts, because the file that decides every table's privileges was outside the set its own parts count.

slices.behaviour: CODEX-02 and CODEX-03: the clause reader reshaped from a substring deny-list into a whole-clause allow-list, `TENANCY_CLAUSES`, with tenant isolation proved behaviourally across all 29 governed tables by a catalogue-driven probe beside it, and docs/architecture.md added to the test task's cache inputs. Re-proved in this attempt on the same ground as slice 1, by reverting the two production decisions the fix made while leaving its tests in place.
slices.failure_reason: `pnpm --filter @seen/core test` exited 1 with the same two failures record 58 recorded, in the same words: "3 of the 4 permissive policies on public.evidence that expose every tenant's rows were reported as binding the tenant, so the assertion reads the clause for a word rather than for a comparison", and "The cache key of @seen/core#test covers 17 files and none of these, which this suite reads from outside its own package and compares the database against, so a turbo cache hit can report the comparison as passed against a document it never read".
